autoWidth:542.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>        As dictated by the tyrannical building codes of Kentucky, all residential and commercial structures are required to maintain functional gutters regardless of the roof's shape or angle.^        These mandated gutters make any pre-existing building a convenient choice for rain water harvesting, allowing you to avoid clambering across the roof to hang up gutter pipes of your own. Some buildings may already have accessible drain pipes on the ground floor needing only a fluid container to complete the system. ^        Simply place the collector on the drain pipe and connect them together with few quick turns of a pipe wrench.<type:text, x:305, y:575, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, pivotX:0, pivotY:0, scaleX:0.5, scaleY:0.5, textLeading:-4, font:SdfOldBold>No drain? No pain!<type:text, x:305, y:605, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:542.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>        If no existing drain pipe is available, an amateur welder could hack together their own using some spare scraps of metal. It doesn't have to be pretty, just water tight!^        Add pipes vertically to extend the drain up as many floors as needed to access the gutters around the roof. Make sure these pipes are properly aligned with the drain and supported by a wall.<type:texture, width:3, height:605, x:535, y:185, pivotX:0, pivotY:0, r:0.3, g:0.3, b:0.3, a:0.5><type:text, x:550, y:180, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:550, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldItalic>PREVIEW: Chapter 3<type:text, x:550, y:200, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, pivotX:0, pivotY:0, scaleX:0.8, scaleY:0.8, textLeading:-4, font:SdfOldBold>Custom-Built ^Structures<type:text, x:550, y:265, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:550, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>        Greedy neighbor unwilling to lend you their roof? Just wanting to get away from it all and carve out your own domain in the forest? The process of harvesting rain water from your own custom-built structure is nearly identical to that of a pre-existing structure, requiring only one additional step to tie it all together. ^        Without those pesky government regulations telling you what to do, you will need to install your own gutter pipes around the outside perimeter of your roof. These can be placed from above or below as long as there is a floor or wall to support them. ^        Watch your step! Thirst will be the least of your problems if you fall.<type:text, x:550, y:575, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, pivotX:0, pivotY:0, scaleX:0.5, scaleY:0.5, textLeading:-4, font:SdfOldBold>Bigger is (Usually) Better<type:text, x:550, y:605, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:542.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>        The larger the roof, the greater the possibilities - up to a point. All drains have a max capacity and any "overflow" will be collected much less effectively. You can build additional drain sections to take full advantage of a large roof but proper spacing is required to avoid over-harvesting from the same areas. Most homes can be fully supported by 1-2 drains while larger buildings may require 3-4 or more for complete coverage. ^        Don't feel intimidated if your home is on the smaller side. Even a one-car garage has enough space to make rain harvesting worthwhile. <type:texture, width:3, height:75, x:25, y:800, pivotX:0, pivotY:0, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.75><type:texture, width:507, height:3, x:28, y:800, pivotX:0, pivotY:0, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.75><type:texture, width:507, height:3, x:28, y:872, pivotX:0, pivotY:0, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.75><type:texture, width:3, height:75, x:535, y:800, pivotX:0, pivotY:0, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.75><type:text, x:70, y:805, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, pivotX:0, pivotY:0, scaleX:0.8, scaleY:0.8, textLeading:-4, font:SdfBold>* CALL NOW *<type:text, x:90, y:840, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, pivotX:0, pivotY:0, scaleX:0.6, scaleY:0.6, textLeading:-4, font:SdfBold>(502) 555-4321<type:text, x:350, y:800, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, pivotX:0, pivotY:0, scaleX:1, scaleY:1, textLeading:-4, font:SdfBold>$19.99<type:text, x:450, y:820, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, pivotX:0, pivotY:0, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, textLeading:-4, font:SdfRegular>x6<type:text, x:350, y:840, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, pivotX:0, pivotY:0, scaleX:0.6, scaleY:0.6, textLeading:-4, font:SdfRegular>Ask for Steve<type:texture, texture:media/textures/printMedia/NewspaperPics/KK_Gradient_1.png, width:789, height:901, pivotX:0.0004, pivotY:0.0004, a:1>

Print_Media_MSC_CabinClimateGuide_info: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD XIV^CABIN CLIMATE<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_climate_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Cabin climate is tied to the engine. Heater uses warm coolant; A/C needs compressor and belt, so comfort can fail because of circulation or accessory problems.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>Use normal heater and A/C controls. Heater works only with warm, sufficient, clean coolant plus a working heater core, pump, and fan belt; A/C needs compressor and belt and becomes stronger at higher engine speed. The blower consumes battery even with engine off. Climate failure removes comfort, not the ability to drive.
Print_Media_MSC_ComponentClassesGuide_in: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD X^COMPONENT CLASSES<type:text, x:105, y:260, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Standard, Heavy-Duty, and Sport are fit classes, not a straight upgrade ladder. A different class can save a found car, but later costs extra wear through compatibility stress.<type:text, x:105, y:460, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:510, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>Read the class before installing a part: Standard, Heavy-Duty, and Sport are compatibility classes, not upgrades. A matching class preserves intended output. A mismatched part still installs, but causes extra wear, heat, fuel use, and stress in linked systems; Diagnostics reports this stress.
Print_Media_MSC_CoolingSystemGuide_info: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD IV^COOLING SYSTEM<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_cooling_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Cooling is one loop: radiator stores liquid, pump circulates it, thermostat directs flow, and fan and belt move heat away. One healthy part cannot save a broken loop.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>In Components, monitor the radiator, water pump, thermostat, fan, hoses, and fan belt as one cooling loop. Low or contaminated coolant, leaks, or a broken belt or pump reduce cooling; heat then damages engine parts and may stop the engine. Replace failed parts and restore correct coolant before driving under load.
Print_Media_MSC_DipstickQuickGuide_info: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD I^OIL DIAGNOSTICS<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_dipstick_sketch_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>A dipstick reads what is happening inside a closed engine without dismantling it. It is a diagnostic tool: oil condition affects pressure and protection of internal components.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>Keep an oil dipstick in your inventory, then open vehicle mechanics and select Fluids. It reveals oil cleanliness and freshness plus coolant and transmission-fluid quality; fluid amount and type remain visible without it. The dipstick only diagnoses—it does not refill or clean a system.
Print_Media_MSC_DrivingLoadGuide_info: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD XII^DRIVING UNDER LOAD<type:text, x:105, y:260, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Overload is not just fast driving: it occurs when the engine requests high power without accelerating the car for too long. That heats vulnerable engine and drivetrain components and accelerates wear.<type:text, x:105, y:460, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:510, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>When high RPM and throttle do not produce acceleration, release throttle or regain speed. Sustained bogging, drivetrain slip, and heavy load build overload after a short grace period; it increases heat and wear in engine and drivetrain parts until normal driving lets it recover. An installed ECU marks overload in Diagnostics.
Print_Media_MSC_ECUDiagnosticsGuide_info: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD XI^ECU DIAGNOSTICS<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_ecu_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>The ECU does not repair a vehicle. It makes hidden simulation data readable, helping separate oil-pressure, cooling, traction, and overload causes.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>In Components → Diagnostics, install a Vehicle ECU from inventory with the hood open and engine stopped. It unlocks the Diagnostics tab and replaces handheld checks with all fluid-quality and temperature readings. Use its live negative-effects list to separate oil-pressure, cooling, drivetrain, compatibility, and overload causes before choosing parts.
Print_Media_MSC_EngineComponentsGuide_in: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD VI^ENGINE COMPONENTS<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_engine_components_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>This is the main MSC work window: the engine is a set of separate components, each with its own installation and removal dependencies. It opens from vanilla vehicle mechanics; right-click Engine → Inspect engine components is an additional route if it did not open automatically.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>The component window opens with vehicle mechanics and an open hood; use Inspect engine components on Engine only to reopen it. Right-click installed parts to remove or empty slots to install a carried part. Tools are mandatory; Mechanics changes success and damage risk rather than blocking work, and the tooltip shows tools, recommended skill, and removal order.
Print_Media_MSC_EngineLiftGuide_info: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD VIII^WORKSHOP LIFT<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_engine_lift_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>A lift does more than speed up work: it turns the engine into a detachable assembly for deep service or swaps. This special operation belongs to the Engine context menu, not the ordinary component list.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>At a complete lift, stop the engine, open the hood, equip a wrench, then right-click Engine → Remove engine at lift or Install engine from lift. Removal places the same assembly on the lift, where it can be inspected and serviced before another car receives it. An empty engine bay stays empty; a cross-family swap works but carries compatibility stress.
Print_Media_MSC_RoadsideRepairGuide_info: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD III^ROADSIDE REPAIRS<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_roadside_repair_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Roadside repair is a short reprieve to reach a workshop, not a complete restoration. Tape, wire, and tools apply to only three components, so use the option carefully.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>With hood open and engine stopped, right-click coolant hoses, fan belt, or ignition coil → Roadside repair. Hoses need duct tape and a screwdriver; the belt needs a wrench; the coil needs wire, tape, and a screwdriver. Repairs are temporary, top out at 60%%, and give less benefit after repeats; only hoses can be saved from 0%% condition.
Print_Media_MSC_RoadsideServiceChecklist: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD II^FLUID SERVICE<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_fluid_service_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Fluids are service resources: they can be drained, mixed, or contaminated. The correct liquid supports its system; a wrong one remains in the reservoir and spoils the mixture.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>In the component window, right-click Oil Pan, Radiator, or Transmission → Manage Fluids. Fill and drain with carried containers; fluids mix, so a wrong liquid remains inside and lowers system purity. Automatic gearboxes need ATF, while manuals need manual transmission oil.
Print_Media_MSC_StartingChargingGuide_in: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD V^STARTING & CHARGING<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_starting_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Starting and charging are separate jobs. Battery and starter begin the engine; alternator and belt return charge while it runs. A car can start without an alternator but cannot run electrical loads for long.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>In Components, check battery, starter, alternator, and fan belt separately. Battery and starter crank the engine; the alternator charges only while its belt turns. A car can start without an alternator, but its battery drains under electrical load and a running engine stops when charge reaches zero.
Print_Media_MSC_TransmissionSetupGuide_i: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD IX^TRANSMISSION SETUP<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_transmission_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>A gearbox transfers power only through the matching coupling. Automatic and manual systems are complete pairs, not interchangeable loose parts: a wrong pair lets the engine run but gives wheels no power.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>Right-click Transmission or Power Coupling in Components. Remove the gearbox and old coupling before changing configuration, then install automatic + torque converter or manual + clutch. A wrong or missing pair lets the engine start but sends no power to wheels; wrong or dirty fluid causes slip, heat, and accelerated wear.
Print_Media_MSC_VehiclePushingGuide_info: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD XIII^PUSH VEHICLE<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_pushing_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Pushing is an emergency way to move a stalled or obstructing car. A heavy vehicle and exhausted character require more effort, while higher Fitness preserves endurance.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>Leave an empty stationary vehicle and stand at its front or rear; right-click it → Push vehicle, or use the bound hotkey. Strength 3 only unlocks the action: more Strength creates a stronger shove and makes it cheaper, while Fitness reduces endurance cost. Heavy vehicles are harder, shown as Effort in the tooltip. Exhaustion blocks pushing and a brief recovery prevents spam.
Print_Media_MSC_WorkshopRebuildGuide_inf: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD VII^REBUILD & SALVAGE<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_workshop_rebuild_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>A removed component is not always scrap. Dismantle it for its material family or rebuild it while retaining exact class and repair history. This makes workshop parts valuable.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>For a removed component, use its inventory actions Dismantle or Repair. Dismantling accepts components at 30%% condition or higher and turns them into the matching material family; healthier parts yield more. Rebuilding needs a work surface, light, tools, and two matching materials. Normal parts repair less effectively each time; legendary parts do not.
